settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic linear bandit with finitely many actions
unmapped: theta* lies in a known convex polytope M with diam(M) <= 1
noise is Gaussian with unit variance in the main model; upper bounds hold for conditionally 1-subgaussian noise
settings.definition_quote: Let $\xX \subset \RR^d$ be a finite set of $k$ actions. We assume that $\xX$ spans $\RR^d$ and $\diam(\xX) \leq 1$. Denote by $\thetaopt \in \mM$ an unknown parameter vector, where $\mM \subset \RR^d$ is a known convex polytope with $\diam(\mM) \leq 1$. ... observes the reward $\y_t = \ip{x_t, \theta} + \epsilon_t$ where $\epsilon_t$ is sampled independently from a Gaussian with zero mean and unit variance. All our upper bounds hold without modification for conditionally $1$-subgaussian noise.

source.label: thm:regret-worstcase
source.quote: \begin{theorem}[Worst-case regret]\label{thm:regret-worstcase} The regret of Algorithm \ref{alg:ids-anytime} is bounded by $R_n \leq \oO\big(d \sqrt{n} \log(n)\big)$.

results.notes: Regret is expected regret with fixed theta*, i.e. pseudo-regret. Horizon n unknown to the algorithm (anytime).

source.label: thm:regret-log
source.quote: \begin{theorem}[Gap-dependent regret]\label{thm:regret-log} The regret of Algorithm \ref{alg:ids-anytime} is bounded by $R_n \leq \oO\left(\Delta_{\min}^{-1} d^3\log(n)^2 \right)$.

results.notes: O hides universal constants and boundedness constants of X and M.

source.label: thm:regret-asymptotic
source.quote: \begin{theorem}[Asymptotic regret]\label{thm:regret-asymptotic} Algorithm \ref{alg:ids-anytime} is asymptotically optimal, $\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{R_n}{\log(n)} = c^*$, where $c^*$ is the solution to the lower bound \eqref{eq:lower-linear} and we assume that $\|x^*\| > 0$.

results.notes: Paper states an exact limit equal to c* (Graves-Lai constant); recorded as limsup R_n/log(T) <= C_lin, matching the lower bound.
